cover.title: Plumbing owners: stop missing sub-zero emergency calls
cover.subtitle: Older homes mean frozen pipes and frantic midnight voicemails.

slides.heading: The midnight freeze rush
slides.body: When temperatures drop, phones start ringing at 2 AM with frozen pipe emergencies. If a call goes to voicemail, the customer hangs up immediately.
slides.tip: Call your own business line after 10 PM tonight. What happens?

slides.heading: Why voicemails get abandoned
slides.body: A homeowner with water leaking through a ceiling will not wait for a morning callback. They simply call the next contractor on the list.

slides.heading: Qualifying the frantic caller
slides.body: Not every late call requires immediate dispatch. Some callers only need shut-off guidance, while active bursts need a technician on the road right away.
slides.tip: Ask: 'Is the main water shut off right now?'

slides.heading: Protecting the morning schedule
slides.body: Capturing job details and reserving the first morning slots overnight keeps your schedule full before your crew clocks in for the day.

slides.heading: Winter call handling recap
slides.body: Answer freeze calls 24/7, collect clear job details right away, and let your technicians focus strictly on repairs when their shift begins.
slides.tip: Review your call log from last weekend and count every call after 8 PM.

caption:
When winter hits, every missed call on a frozen pipe goes straight to the next shop down the road.

Capturing after-hours emergency calls keeps your schedule full without waking up your technicians or burning out your office team.
